headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Botpress to Superset via shared content flow; prompt injection and cascading errors are otherwise limited by missing shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress can ingest and emit conversational content, and Superset can consume API-driven inputs, but neither profile shows a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge. The pairwise injection path is therefore plausible only through manual or external bridging, not by default. Uncertainty remains because both are unverified docs-only profiles.
conditions: IF an operator copies Botpress output into Superset inputs without review, prompt injection becomes actionable.
IF a shared workspace, clipboard bridge, or MCP server is added, the risk increases.
mitigations: Require manual review before pasting Botpress output into Superset.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared workspace between the two systems.
Add a provenance tag to Botpress-generated text before reuse.
Use a fixed template in Superset that strips instructions from imported text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent and Superset is a data-engineering/BI system with API access; a shared workflow can move sensitive support or analytics content between them. Botpress has network egress none, but Superset has allowlisted egress and API surfaces, so leakage risk exists in default integrations even though no secrets are explicitly listed. The exact data classes are undocumented, so severity stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs customer records or tickets into Superset dashboards or queries, those data may be exposed beyond the original support context.
IF Superset API calls include imported Botpress transcripts, the transcripts can be retained or redistributed.
mitigations: Restrict Botpress-to-Superset transfers to redacted fields only.
Review Superset API payloads for sensitive text before enabling sync.
Turn off any automatic transcript export from Botpress.
Use separate service accounts for each system.
requires-engineering: implement field-level data loss prevention at the integration layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while Superset exposes API calls and allowlisted egress, but neither profile shows unrestricted shared filesystem writes, git mutation, or overlapping OAuth scopes. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Because the profiles are unverified and concurrency details are empty, uncertainty is resolved upward only to low, not none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or database, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Keep Botpress and Superset on separate writable directories.
Avoid sharing a database or git repository between them.
Run each under distinct service accounts.
Check for overlapping API write scopes before integration.
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate support content that Superset may ingest through its API surfaces, creating a plausible path where B treats A’s output as authoritative. No verification or critique mechanism is documented in either profile, so a bad Botpress answer can cascade into Superset reports or actions. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than irreversible by default.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards or workflows consume Botpress-generated text without validation, errors can propagate.
IF Botpress is used to summarize facts that Superset later renders as authoritative, downstream decisions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of Botpress outputs before Superset ingestion.
Add a validation step in Superset for any Botpress-derived fields.
Label Botpress content as untrusted in downstream reports.
Limit Botpress output to summaries, not factual assertions.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or schema validation before Superset uses Botpress content.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit PHI, residency, or retention commitments listed. That means a compliance breach is not evidenced, but the pair could still create policy mismatch if support data from Botpress is moved into Superset analytics. Because no jurisdictional or certification mismatch is documented, severity remains low.
conditions: IF regulated support data is exported from Botpress into Superset, retention and access policies must be checked.
IF either deployment stores EU PII or PHI, residency and certification requirements must be verified.
mitigations: Inventory the data classes each system will handle.
Confirm retention settings in both deployments.
Separate regulated data from general analytics.
Document the lawful basis for any cross-system transfer.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for residency and retention at the pipeline boundary.
